programme: MAZ and MEF2D are DNA-binding transcription factors whose output depends on which cofactor they partner — corepressor complexes (class IIa HDACs such as HDAC7) versus coactivators of the NCOA2/CREBBP-p160 family. In sarcoma this exact partnering logic is fixed genetically by chromosomal fusion: MAZ::NCOA2, MEF2D::NCOA2, GLI2::CREBBP and PAX3::MYOCD each yoke a DNA-binding domain to a coactivator domain, producing constitutively active fusion oncoproteins that define distinct mesenchymal tumor subtypes. SMARCE1 (core BAF/SWI-SNF subunit) and KAT7/HBO1 (histone acetyltransferase) sit on the same coactivator-complex axis — SMARCE1 stabilizes the mutant BAF complex in SS18::SSX synovial sarcoma, KAT7 is oncogenically overexpressed in osteosarcoma.
role_in_a: MEF2D is a pro-survival neuronal transcription factor that GSK3β inactivates by phosphorylation, tipping it toward corepression and neuronal apoptosis relevant to AD neurodegeneration; this is rescued by galangin in an APP/PS1 mouse model. MAZ physically interacts with FAC1 (the Alz-50 antigen), a chromatin-associated protein that abnormally accumulates in AD-affected neurons, placing MAZ within the chromatin apparatus disturbed in AD.
role_in_b: MAZ, MEF2D, GLI2 and MYOCD are recurrent fusion-oncogene partners: MAZ::NCOA2, MEF2D::NCOA2, GLI2::CREBBP and PAX3::MYOCD each constitutively activate coactivator-recruiting transcription and define specific sarcoma/soft-tissue-tumor subtypes. SMARCE1 and KAT7 are independently oncogenic through the same coactivator/chromatin-complex logic — SMARCE1 in SS18::SSX-driven synovial sarcoma, KAT7/HBO1 in osteosarcoma.
shared_axis: Both diseases put pressure on the same corepressor-versus-coactivator switch that governs MAZ- and MEF2D-class transcription factors: physiologically it decides neuronal survival or death in AD, and when the switch is fixed permanently by chromosomal translocation it becomes an oncogenic engine in sarcoma. No retrieved paper shows this switch operating in both tissues at once — the link is inferred from the shared cofactor logic, not observed directly.
reasoning: The sarcoma side of the module is unusually well evidenced — six of the twelve concordant factors have direct fusion/oncogene papers naming them by exactly this coactivator-hijacking mechanism. The AD side rests on only two old, narrow findings (a single 2000 protein-interaction paper for MAZ, a phosphorylation/mouse-model pair for MEF2D), and a related factor (TP73) returned an explicit negative finding for AD, so the cross-disease connection is argued from shared molecular logic rather than shown by any retrieved source.
support: PMID 41245811 — MAZ::NCOA2 fusion defines an intracranial sarcoma subtype; PMID 39985329 — MAZ::NCOA2 fusion in subcutaneous small round cell sarcoma of infancy; PMID 41107857 — MAZ acts downstream of pentraxin-3 in osteosarcoma metastasis; PMID 10727212 — MAZ interacts with FAC1/Alz-50 antigen, a chromatin protein implicated in AD-affected neurons; PMID 40057039 — MEF2D::NCOA2 fusion defines vulvovaginal myxoid epithelioid tumor; PMID 31754707 — class IIa HDAC (HDAC7) repressive complexes regulate epigenetic responses in a sarcoma-relevant context, consistent with MEF2D's corepressor side; PMID 19801631 — GSK3β phosphorylates MEF2D, inactivating its pro-survival transcription and driving neuronal apoptosis; PMID 35718493 — galangin alleviates memory impairment in APP/PS1 Alzheimer's mice via this signaling axis; PMID 42068354 — GLI2::CREBBP fusion defines nested-hyalinizing epithelioid soft tissue tumors; PMID 39970333 — GLI2 drives immune evasion/immunotherapy resistance in sarcoma; PMID 40813503 — GLI1/2-altered mesenchymal tumor series; PMID 34697065 — PAX3-MYOCD fusion in pediatric rhabdomyosarcoma; PMID 41193430 — SMARCE1/SUMOylation targeting destabilizes the mutant SS18::SSX BAF complex in synovial sarcoma; PMID 33754016 — KAT7/HBO1 is oncogenic in osteosarcoma; PMID 23414597 — direct test of TP73 in AD found no association (negative evidence, weighs against extending the module to AD).
how_to_falsify: Compare MAZ and MEF2D chromatin occupancy and target-gene activation in AD-model neurons (or post-mortem AD brain) against their occupancy at fusion-activated loci in MAZ::NCOA2/MEF2D::NCOA2 sarcoma lines. If the neuronal target sets do not overlap with the fusion-activated target sets, and if HDAC7/NCOA2-CREBBP occupancy at MEF2D or MAZ sites is unchanged between AD and control brain tissue, the proposed shared corepressor/coactivator-switch axis is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain versus soft tissue with no anatomical overlap; the sarcoma evidence is recent and disease-specific (fusion-defined tumor subtypes) while the AD evidence is old, sparse, and indirect. TP73 was excluded from the carrying set because its only direct AD paper reports a lack of association, and it should not be leaned on. Five single-view factors (LMX1B, SOX10, MXD4, UBTF, NCOA4) were dropped as one-cohort artifacts; note SOX10 both topped a single group and sits on the tissue-generic exclusion list, so its absence is by design. HDAC7 and NOTCH1 — both mechanistically adjacent to this story (HDAC7 corepresses MEF2D; NOTCH1 is a JARID2 target) — were removed as generic to brain/soft tissue, so the account cannot lean on them even though they would fit.
